skill.name: storyboard-creation
skill.description: Plan film and video storyboards with shot vocabulary, camera direction, continuity guidance, annotated panels, and optional AI image generation through the belt CLI.
skill.summary: Build clear shot lists, annotated panels, and consistent visual storyboards.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline formatting. Six findings contain intended belt or npx commands, while semantic review identified unpinned installations and third-party processing of prompts or images. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Remote CLI and skill installation commands are not pinned to immutable versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted package versions or commit references and ask users to review each source before installation.

remediation.issue: Storyboard prompts and image inputs may be processed by an external inference service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external service, its data handling terms, and advise users to exclude confidential material.

content.value_statement: Turning a script into coherent shots requires precise framing, continuity, and annotation. This skill guides shot planning and optional AI panel generation.
actual_capabilities: Defines common shot types, framing, and recommended uses.
Explains camera angles, movements, and their narrative effects.
Applies the 180-degree rule, match on action, eyeline match, and screen direction.
Structures shot lists and annotated storyboard panels.
Provides belt CLI examples for consistent landscape panel generation.
Provides commands for stitching panels into rows and complete boards.
limitations: AI image generation requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and external service access.
The skill does not create timed animatics, edit footage, or produce audio.
Generated character and style continuity depend on the selected model and prompts.
Image examples use fixed landscape dimensions and require adaptation for other formats.

use_cases.title: Plan a Narrative Scene
use_cases.description: Convert a scene into varied shots with clear framing, movement, duration, action, and sound notes.

use_cases.title: Present an Advertising Concept
use_cases.description: Build a concise visual sequence that communicates product beats and camera choices before production.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Animation Sequence
use_cases.description: Map action, eyelines, screen direction, and panel continuity for review by an animation team.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a six-shot storyboard for [SCENE]. Include shot type, angle, action, duration, and one continuity note per shot.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a first storyboard outline.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Script Excerpt
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this script excerpt into an annotated shot list: [SCRIPT]. Vary framing and identify dialogue, sound effects, and camera movement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a script already exists.

prompt_templates.title: Design Consistent AI Panels
prompt_templates.prompt: Create image prompts for each shot in [SHOT LIST]. Keep character details, lens, lighting, color grade, style, and aspect ratio consistent.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before generating panels with an image service.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Continuity and Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this storyboard: [STORYBOARD]. Find axis crossings, eyeline errors, screen-direction reversals, missing coverage, pacing problems, and weak transitions. Propose precise revisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for an advanced production review.

output_examples.input: Storyboard a short office scene where Sarah discovers an unexpected letter.
output: 1.1 WS, eye level, static, 3 seconds: Establish the office as Sarah enters.
1.2 MS, eye level, tracking, 4 seconds: Follow Sarah toward her desk.
1.3 ECU, high angle, static, 2 seconds: Reveal the unfamiliar handwriting on the envelope.
1.4 CU, eye level, slow dolly in, 3 seconds: Show Sarah reacting as she reads.

output_examples.input: Review two dialogue shots filmed from opposite sides of the actors.
output_examples.output: The cut may cross the 180-degree axis and reverse screen positions. Keep both cameras on one side or insert a neutral transition shot.

output_examples.input: Suggest a compact board layout for six detailed dialogue panels.
output_examples.output: Use a 2x3 layout. Label every panel with shot type, angle, movement, duration, action, dialogue, sound effects, and music.

best_practices: Start each scene with a clear establishing shot before moving to tighter coverage.
Keep lens, lighting, color grade, character details, and aspect ratio consistent across generated panels.
Annotate every panel with production details that the crew can interpret without guessing.
anti_patterns: Do not use the same shot size for every panel.
Do not cross the 180-degree axis without a motivated transition or visible camera move.
Do not send confidential scripts or images to external services without approval.

faq.question: Does this skill generate storyboard images?
faq.answer: It provides prompts and belt CLI examples. Image generation requires an inference.sh account and access to the listed applications.

faq.question: Can I use the planning guidance without the CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Shot vocabulary, continuity rules, layouts, annotations, and workflow guidance work without image generation.

faq.question: Which storyboard layouts are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, and single-panel layouts.

faq.question: Will generated characters remain consistent?
faq.answer: Consistency is not guaranteed. Reuse detailed character descriptions and style settings, then regenerate mismatched panels.

faq.question: Can I create vertical or mobile storyboards?
faq.answer: Yes, but the command examples use landscape dimensions. Adjust aspect ratio, composition, and panel layout for vertical delivery.

faq.question: Which continuity checks are included?
faq.answer: The guidance covers the 180-degree rule, match on action, eyeline match, and consistent screen direction.
